newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila SEC orders probe on share price surges.
newsitem.headline: Manila SEC orders probe on share price surges.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission has ordered the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) to investigate the sharp price rises in several penny stocks over the past weeks, SEC chairman Perfecto Yasay said on Tuesday.
"There is a possibility of insiders' trading. There is also a possibility that market players are manipulating the prices," Yasay told reporters.

"Right now, we have very preliminary reports. We have not yet decided if there are already some guilty parties since the PSE has not yet submitted a formal report to us on the results of their investigations," he added.
The bourse was ordered to conduct thorough investigations on who were punting the speculative issues, mostly dormant oil and mining companies, he added.
A flurry of buying in rarely-traded issues has recently provided some excitement in the local stock market.
At present, the bourse freezes a share price if it reaches the limit of a 50 percent rise within a single day. The price freeze is lifted the next trading day.

Among the companies which had reached their daily limits are Acoje Holdings Corp, which rose to a high of 59 centavos from 16 centavos in just four sessions; Marsteel Corp, up to 6.0 centavos from 2.1 centavos in one week; Itogon Suyoc Mines Inc, up to 24.50 centavos from 2.50 centavos in two weeks.
When asked to explain, company officials said they did not know of any material information which could explain the price movement.
Insider trading is punishable in the Philippines by a jail term of 15 to 20 years. So far, nobody has been jailed for insider trading in the Philippines.
